name: TOGO
lead: Togo is a thin slice of West Africa. You can drive across it in an hour. Lomé, the capital, sits on a beach. It has mud tower-houses, the world's biggest voodoo market, and forest elephants.

sections.geography: A very thin strip of land
sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Togo is one of the world's narrowest countries. At its slimmest it is only 56 km wide. It stretches 560 km, from the Gulf of Guinea (a bay of the Atlantic) to dry savanna by Burkina Faso.
Going north, sandy coast turns into rolling plateaus. Then the Togo Mountains rise. Mont Agou, at 986 m, is the tallest peak.
animals: Fazao-Malfakassa National Park has about 60 savanna elephants. They are the most westerly ones in the Guinea savanna. Patas monkeys, baboons, and roan antelopes live there too.
The park has over 244 bird species. Hippos and crocodiles live in the southern rivers.
culture: The Ewe people weave kente cloth, stitching bright strips into festival robes. Their drumming layers many beats at once. Musicians study it in universities worldwide.
Vodun (voodoo) is an officially recognised religion. Lomé's Akodessewa is the world's largest voodoo market. Each year, the Yam Festival celebrates the harvest with food and dance.
history: Germany claimed Togoland in 1884. It built a railway and Lomé's port. In 1914, British and French forces captured it in 26 days. It was the first win for Britain and France in World War I.
France governed the eastern half until 27 April 1960. Then Togo became independent. In 2004, Koutammakou, with its mud tower-houses, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site (a protected place).
wows: In Lomé, you can walk from Togo into Ghana.
Togo has the world's 4th-largest phosphate reserves, used in fertiliser (plant food).
Lomé's voodoo market, Earth's largest, supplies healers across West Africa.
Germany built one of Africa's earliest railways in Togo in the 1900s.
The Batammariba people build mud tower-houses, called takienta, in a design over 300 years old.
Artist Paul Ahyi designed the flag in 1960; its five stripes stand for five regions.
Ewe drumming is so tricky that universities in the USA and Europe teach it.

myths.myth: Voodoo is all about evil spells
myths.fact: Vodun is about ancestors, healing, and community. Movies made it look scary.
It began in West Africa. Enslaved people later carried it across the ocean to Haiti.
